You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

def f(g):
    h=len(g); w=len(g[0])
    out=[row[:] for row in g]
    # 5s are the "bars"; pattern = non-zero non-5 cells
    cells=[(i,j,g[i][j]) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j] not in (0,5)]
    # group pattern cells into connected components (orthogonal)
    comps=[]; seen=set()
    for c in cells:
        if c[:2] in seen: continue
        st=[c]; comp=[]
        while st:
            a,b,v=st.pop()
            if (a,b) in seen: continue
            seen.add((a,b)); comp.append((a,b,v))
            for d in [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)]:
                x,y=a+d[0],b+d[1]
                if 0<=x<h and 0<=y<w and g[x][y] not in (0,5) and (x,y) not in seen:
                    st.append((x,y,g[x][y]))
        comps.append(comp)
    # a "strip" component is a straight line of distinct values (single color per row/col run); pattern block = larger
    def is_strip(c):
        rs=[a for a,b,v in c]; cs=[b for a,b,v in c]
        if len(rs)==len(set(rs))==1 and len(cs)>1: return True   # horizontal run of one color... pattern row "868" has two colors
        return False
    def horiz_run(c): return max(rs)<=min(rs)+0 and len(cs)>1
    def vert_run(c): return max(cs)<=min(cs)+0 and len(rs)>1
    def stripe(c): return (max(rs)<=min(rs)+0 and len(cs)>1) or (max(cs)<=min(cs)+0 and len(rs)>1)
    def pattern_block(c): return not stripe(c) and len(c)>1
    bars5=[(i,j) for i in range(h) for j in range(w) if g[i][j]==5]
    bset=set(bars5)
    def adj5(c):
        s=set((a,b) for a,b,v in c)
        return sum(1 for a,b,v in c for dx,dy in [(1,0),(-1,0),(0,1),(0,-1)] if (a+dx,b+dy) in bset)
    # components touching the 5s are candidates
    P=[comp for comp in comps if adj5(comp)==len(comp)]
    if len(P)!=1:
        # try largest non-strip component as pattern
        P=[max(comps,key=len)]
    for comp in P:
        vals={v for _,_,v in comp}
        if len(vals)>1: continue  # single-color strip is not the pattern source (those are lines like "8 6 8")
    # actually pattern block: multi-colored. find components with >1 color and touching 5s
    P=[comp for comp in comps if len({v for _,_,v in comp})>1]
    if not P: P=None
    if P is None:
        print("no pattern"); return out
    P=max(P,key=len)
    ps=[(a,b) for a,b,_ in P]
    rs=[a for a,b in ps]; cs=[b for a,b in ps]
    r0,r1,c0,c1=min(rs),max(rs),min(cs),max(cs)
    ph,pw=r1-r0+1,c1-c0+1
    pat=[[g[r0+di][c0+dj] for dj in range(pw)] for di in range(ph)]
    # direction of fill: perpendicular to the bar orientation next to the pattern
    # determine bar orientation: if 5s immediately left of pattern cells -> vertical bar (fill rows) ; horizontal bar above -> fill cols
    # check: number of 5-neighbors to the left vs above of pattern cells
    nb_left=sum(1 for a,b in ps if (a,b-1) in bset)
    nb_up=sum(1 for a,b in ps if (a-1,b) in bset)
    if nb_left>nb_up:
        # vertical bar on left: fill upward from r0-1 to line top
        vline=next(j for j in range(w) if all((a,j) in bset for a in range(h)))
        top=[i for i in range(h) if (i,vline) in bset]
        t0,t1=min(top),max(top)
        for i in range(t0,min(r0,h)):
            for jj in range(c0,c1+1):
                if g[i][jj]==0:
                    out[i][jj]=pat[(i-r0)%ph][jj-c0]
    else:
        # horizontal bar above pattern: fill rightward from c1+1? demo3: bar row1 cols1-6, pattern col0 rows2-7 (left of bar). fill cols c0..c_bar_end? demo3 bar is BELOW-left... 
        pass
    return out
